Why monitor bus bars

Joint failures build up quietly, then fail suddenly

Most bus-bar faults start at a joint. Periodic manual thermography only catches the problem if someone happens to look on the right day.

  • OverheatingJoints run hot under load, often with no visible sign until insulation or copper is damaged.
  • CorrosionOxidised contact surfaces raise joint resistance, which raises temperature over time.
  • Loose connectionsBolts loosen with vibration and thermal cycling, creating hot spots at the joint.
→
Which leads to
  • Difficult manual thermal inspection
  • Risk of fire hazards
  • Possibility of unplanned downtimes
  • Greater energy losses

That is why plants need a real-time solution that puts bus-bar temperature data online, so these problems are caught and fixed early.

How it works

From joint to phone in five steps

No wiring to the hot side: the straps are battery powered and talk wirelessly to a receiver in the panel.

  1. 01Sensor strapsOne per phase (R · Y · B), strapped on each critical jointRF signal · 10 m range →
    RF signal · 10 m range
  2. 02ReceiverCollects readings from up to 60 sensors in the panelModbus RS-485 →
    Modbus RS-485
  3. 03IoT gatewayST-52 C on 4G, Ethernet or Wi-Fi, with local backup storageSecure upload →
    Secure upload
  4. 04Cloud platformI/O Sense stores data, checks limits and raises critical alertsDashboards & alerts →
    Dashboards & alerts
  5. 05Laptop / mobileLive view, alerts, trends and reports for the maintenance team

Online continuous monitoring with critical alerts helps avert major losses, increase safety and improve the upkeep of electrical operations.

Wireless bus-bar sensor strap

A battery-powered digital temperature sensor on a heat-proof strap, fitted directly on the bus-bar joint. Colour coded by phase.

Mounted in or near the panel. Listens to the sensor straps over RF and passes their readings to the gateway on Modbus.

I/O Sense platform

One screen for every joint in the plant

Live status, alerts, trends and reports for the electrical and maintenance teams, on laptop or mobile.

How many joints are at normal, warning or critical temperature, and how many sensor batteries need attention. A live table shows incomer and outgoing temperatures for each phase of every feeder.

Every high-temperature and above-ambient event, with the device, start and stop time and how long it lasted. Exportable for maintenance records.

Each feeder’s R, Y and B phase temperatures over any date range, so a joint that is slowly heating up stands out before it fails.

Scheduled reports of average phase temperatures per feeder, ready to share with the electrical and maintenance teams.
